day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver International Airport at 12:00 PM on Flight AC. Collect luggage and take the Canada Line SkyTrain directly from YVR Airport station to downtown Vancouver — a budget-friendly ~$4 CAD fare. Check in to Vancouver Harbour Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Granville Island Public Market Food Tour (self-guided to save money). Stroll through the iconic market sampling local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, baked goods, and seasonal produce. Pick up affordable bites from the many vendor stalls for a late lunch. Explore the surrounding Granville Island arts district on foot — free to wander.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take a short bus ride along the waterfront back toward the harbour area. Explore the Gastown neighbourhood — admire the famous Steam Clock and cobblestone streets at no cost. Wind down with a relaxed evening near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and snack at the airport or on the SkyTrain — budget ~$5 CAD
meals.lunch: Self-guided tasting lunch at Granville Island Public Market — mix of vendor samples and a fresh item like a salmon roll or artisan sandwich — budget ~$12–15 CAD
meals.dinner: Steamworks Brew Pub in Gastown for a budget-friendly burger and local craft beer, or grab a hearty bowl from one of the affordable Vietnamese pho spots on Robson Street — budget ~$15–18 CAD

day_by_day.notes: Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR to downtown is the most budget-friendly airport transfer (~$4 CAD with a Compass Card). Pick up a reloadable Compass Card at the airport for all transit during the trip. Granville Island is best explored on foot — take Bus 50 from downtown or walk across the Burrard Bridge.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning ride along the Stanley Park Seawall. Rent a bike from Spokes Bicycle Rentals near the park entrance (~$8–12 CAD/hour or ~$30 for a half-day). Cycle the stunning 10km seawall loop around Stanley Park, enjoying views of the North Shore mountains, Lions Gate Bridge, and English Bay. Stop at Siwash Rock and Prospect Point Lookout — all free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return the bike and explore Stanley Park on foot — visit the free Totem Poles at Brockton Point and enjoy a picnic lunch in the park. Afterwards, walk or bus to Denman Street in the West End for window shopping and local neighbourhood vibes.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a golden-hour sunset at English Bay Beach — one of Vancouver's most beloved free experiences. Grab takeout and eat on the beach for a relaxed, budget-friendly evening.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh bagel and coffee from a local café near the hotel — budget ~$6–8 CAD
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a nearby grocery store (Save-On-Foods or IGA) before heading to Stanley Park — fresh fruit, deli items, and drinks for ~$10–12 CAD
meals.dinner: Grab affordable Japanese takeout (bento box or sushi roll combo) from a spot on Robson Street, or try Davie Street's budget-friendly international eateries — budget ~$12–16 CAD

day_by_day.notes: Stanley Park is free to enter. Bike rentals from Spokes Bicycle Rentals on West Georgia Street are the most budget-friendly option near the park. Bring sunscreen and a light jacket as June weather near the water can be breezy even on warm days.

day_by_day.morning: Take a TransLink bus to Lynn Canyon Park for the Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre experience. The suspension bridge and park are completely FREE — a fantastic alternative to the pricier Capilano Suspension Bridge. Cross the bridge over the dramatic canyon, hike the Twin Falls Trail through old-growth forest, and visit the free Ecology Centre to learn about the local ecosystem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Lynn Canyon's network of hiking trails — the Baden Powell Trail section offers beautiful forest scenery at no cost. Pack a lunch to enjoy creekside in the park. Head back to Vancouver in the mid-afternoon via bus and SkyTrain.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Commercial Drive neighbourhood ('The Drive') — a vibrant, eclectic, and very budget-friendly area known for its independent cafés, murals, and diverse food scene. Browse the local shops and enjoy the neighbourhood atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal or toast at the hotel if available, or a budget breakfast sandwich from a local café — budget ~$5–7 CAD
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch from a grocery store the night before — sandwiches, trail mix, fruit, and water — budget ~$8–10 CAD
meals.dinner: Dinner on Commercial Drive — try La Mezcaleria for affordable tacos, or grab a slice from one of the neighbourhood's beloved independent pizza spots — budget ~$12–15 CAD

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon is accessible via SkyTrain (Expo Line to Lonsdale Quay, then Bus 229) — total transit cost with Compass Card ~$6–8 CAD round trip. The free suspension bridge and trails make this a top budget nature experience in Vancouver. Wear sturdy walking shoes and bring water.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Capilano River Regional Park for a self-led Forest Bathing Walk through the towering Douglas firs along the Capilano Pacific Trail — completely free. Practice mindful walking, breathe in the forest air, and enjoy the serene riverside environment. This is a peaceful and restorative way to spend the final morning in Vancouver.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to downtown Vancouver and spend your last afternoon revisiting favourite spots or exploring Chinatown — one of North America's oldest and most vibrant Chinese neighbourhoods. Visit the free Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden courtyard (the garden itself costs ~$14 CAD but the adjacent park is free). Browse Chinatown's affordable shops and markets.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Vancouver — treat yourself to a slightly nicer but still budget-conscious meal to celebrate the trip. Head back to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Grab a hearty breakfast burrito or banh mi from a local spot near the hotel to fuel the morning hike — budget ~$7–9 CAD
meals.lunch: Dim sum lunch in Chinatown — many restaurants offer excellent value lunch specials with steamed dumplings, rice noodle rolls, and more — budget ~$12–15 CAD
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a beloved local spot — try Phnom Penh Restaurant in Chinatown (cash only, legendary butter beef and chicken wings) for an authentic, affordable, and memorable Vancouver meal — budget ~$16–20 CAD

day_by_day.notes: Capilano River Regional Park is accessible via Bus 236 from downtown — free park entry. Phnom Penh Restaurant is a Vancouver institution and very popular — arrive early or expect a short wait. If departing the following morning, confirm hotel checkout time and arrange airport transport via Canada Line SkyTrain for the most budget-friendly option.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Vancouver International Airport at 12:00 PM on flight AC. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Canada Line SkyTrain directly from YVR to downtown Vancouver (approx. 25 min, ~$4 CAD). Check in to Vancouver Harbour Stay and freshen up. Take a leisurely walk along the Coal Harbour seawall to shake off travel fatigue and soak in your first views of the North Shore mountains and marina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Stanley Park for a relaxed introductory visit. Stroll or rent a bike ($15–20/hr) and explore a portion of the iconic 10km seawall. Enjoy views of Lions Gate Bridge, Siwash Rock, and English Bay. Stop at Prospect Point Lookout for panoramic photos. Keep the pace easy given the late arrival morning.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Robson Street and Davie Village for dinner. Wind down with a walk along English Bay Beach to watch the sunset over the Pacific — one of Vancouver's most beloved free experiences.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and snack at a café near the airport or on the SkyTrain corridor upon arrival — try Waves Coffee or Tim Hortons in the terminal.
meals.lunch: Pick up a casual bite near the hotel at The Templeton on Granville St (classic diner, ~$15–20 CAD) or grab a poke bowl from Pokéworks on Robson Street.
meals.dinner: Miku Restaurant on the waterfront near Coal Harbour — renowned for aburi (flame-seared) sushi with local Pacific ingredients. Budget ~$50–70/person for a mid-range splurge to celebrate arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at noon, Day 1 is intentionally relaxed. No pre-booked morning tours. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance — many allow early check-in for a fee or luggage storage if the room isn't ready. Grab a Compass Card at the airport SkyTrain station for convenient transit use throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with the Granville Island Public Market Food Tour. Arrive at Granville Island by 9:30 AM via the False Creek Aquabus ferry from downtown (~$4 one-way, a fun mini-experience in itself). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the market — sample local artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, baked goods, and charcuterie from various vendors. This doubles as a delicious brunch experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, browse Granville Island's artisan studios and independent shops. Cross back to downtown and head to Kitsilano (Kits Beach) for a relaxing afternoon. Rent a kayak or SUP board from Ecomarine ($30–45/hr) for a paddle on English Bay with mountain backdrop views, or simply relax on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Main Street / Mount Pleasant neighbourhood for dinner and local craft beer. Explore the independent boutiques and street art along Main Street before settling in for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or a quick coffee at Revolver Coffee (top-rated specialty café) on Cambie Street before heading to Granville Island.
meals.lunch: Graze through the Granville Island Public Market stalls — build a meal from vendor samples: smoked salmon from Longliner Seafoods, fresh bread from Terra Breads, and fruit from local produce stands. Budget ~$20–30 CAD.
meals.dinner: The Acorn on Main Street — acclaimed plant-forward restaurant with locally sourced ingredients and creative cocktails. Great for food lovers seeking something unique. Budget ~$40–55/person.

day_by_day.notes: Granville Island is busiest on weekends — a Tuesday visit means lighter crowds and a more authentic local experience. The Aquabus runs frequently from the Hornby Street dock downtown. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a reusable bag for any market purchases. Check if the food tour is self-guided or operator-led and book in advance if the latter.

day_by_day.morning: Full nature day on the North Shore. Take a bus or rideshare (~20–30 min from downtown) to Lynn Canyon Park for the Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre experience. The suspension bridge is free (unlike Capilano) and equally thrilling. Hike through old-growth forest trails, visit the Ecology Centre to learn about local ecosystems, and enjoy the canyon views. Arrive by 9:00 AM to beat midday crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Lynn Canyon, travel a short distance to Capilano River Regional Park for the Forest Bathing Walk. Spend 1.5–2 hours in a self-led forest bathing (Shinrin-yoku) experience along the riverside trails beneath towering Douglas firs. This is a free, meditative complement to the morning's more active hiking. The contrast of the two parks makes for a rich, full nature immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to downtown Vancouver via transit. Spend the evening exploring Gastown — Vancouver's oldest neighbourhood — with its cobblestone streets, steam clock, and vibrant dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before departing at Jam Café on Beatty Street (popular brunch spot, arrive early or expect a short wait) — ~$18–25 CAD. Or pick up pastries from a nearby bakery for an on-the-go option.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a grocery store (Choices Markets or Save-On-Foods) the night before — sandwiches, fruit, trail mix — ideal for eating trailside at Lynn Canyon. Budget ~$12–15 CAD.
meals.dinner: Pidgin Restaurant in Gastown — modern Canadian-Asian fusion with locally sourced proteins and seasonal vegetables. Buzzy atmosphere and excellent cocktails. Budget ~$45–60/person.

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon Park is free to enter — a great mid-range budget win. Wear sturdy hiking shoes and bring layers as forest trails can be cool even in June. The Capilano River Regional Park is easily accessible by TransLink bus (Bus 236 from Lonsdale Quay). Consider taking the SeaBus from downtown to North Vancouver's Lonsdale Quay (~$4) for a scenic harbour crossing — it's a local experience in itself. Bring water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Stanley Park for the full Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Picnic experience. Rent bikes from Spokes Bicycle Rentals at the park entrance (~$15–20/hr) by 9:00 AM and complete the full 10km seawall loop. Stop at Beaver Lake, the totem poles at Brockton Point, and Second Beach. The morning light on the mountains and harbour is spectacular. Lock up bikes and enjoy a picnic at Second Beach or Lost Lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Richmond for the Richmond Night Market & Authentic Asian Street Food experience. Richmond's Golden Village (No. 3 Road area) is a world-class destination for authentic Asian cuisine. Spend the afternoon exploring T&T Supermarket (a fascinating Asian grocery experience), Aberdeen Centre, and the surrounding food scene. If visiting in the evening, the Richmond Night Market runs seasonally May–October and is a must.
day_by_day.evening: Return to downtown for a final evening stroll along the Coal Harbour waterfront near the hotel. Reflect on the trip with a drink at a rooftop bar or waterfront patio. Consider visiting the Vancouver Lookout Tower (~$20 CAD) for a 360° sunset panorama of the city before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café Medina on Beatty Street — beloved Vancouver institution famous for Belgian waffles and Mediterranean-inspired brunch. Budget ~$20–28 CAD. Book ahead or arrive early.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Stanley Park — pick up supplies from Urban Fare on Alberni Street (gourmet grocery) the morning of: sandwiches, local cheeses, sparkling water, and fresh fruit. Budget ~$20–25 CAD.
meals.dinner: Richmond Night Market food stalls for a festive final dinner — try takoyaki, Taiwanese stinky tofu, BBQ skewers, mango shaved ice, and Hong Kong egg waffles from various vendors. An adventurous, affordable, and memorable way to end the trip. Budget ~$20–35 CAD for a full spread.

day_by_day.notes: The Richmond Night Market typically runs Thursday–Sunday evenings (5 PM–midnight) in summer — a Thursday visit works perfectly. Entry fee is ~$5 CAD. Take the Canada Line SkyTrain from downtown to Bridgeport Station (Richmond) — about 25 minutes and very convenient. Bring cash as some stalls prefer it. This final day balances active outdoor adventure in the morning with a vibrant multicultural food experience in the evening — a perfect Vancouver send-off.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight AC lands at 12:00 PM. Transfer by private car service to Vancouver Harbour Stay. Take time to settle in, freshen up, and enjoy the harbour views from your room. No morning activities scheduled prior to arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour: Head to the iconic Granville Island Public Market (approx. 15-min drive or scenic False Creek ferry from downtown). Sample artisan cheeses, fresh Pacific salmon, house-made charcuterie, and local pastries from award-winning vendors. Stroll the artisan studios and pick up gourmet provisions. This is a perfect soft introduction to Vancouver's celebrated food scene.
day_by_day.evening: Waterfront Dining & Harbour Stroll: Enjoy a leisurely evening walk along the Coal Harbour seawall directly from your hotel, taking in views of the North Shore mountains and marina. Cap the night with a world-class dinner at a top waterfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: N/A – mid-day arrival. Grab a light snack or coffee upon landing.
meals.lunch: Granville Island Public Market grazing: curated tasting spread of local charcuterie, artisan bread, Pacific smoked salmon, and fresh-pressed juice from market vendors (~$40–60 pp).
meals.dinner: Ancora Waterfront Dining & Patio (Coal Harbour) – Peruvian-Japanese inspired seafood with stunning harbour views. Try the Wagyu beef tataki and whole roasted halibut. Reserve in advance. (~$120–160 pp with wine pairing).

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance through your hotel concierge for a seamless arrival experience. The False Creek Aquabus ferry from downtown to Granville Island is a scenic and fun option in the afternoon. June evenings in Vancouver are long and mild – perfect for a waterfront walk after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Picnic: Start the day early with a premium bike rental (or arrange a guided private cycling experience) and ride the breathtaking 10km seawall around Stanley Park. Pass Siwash Rock, Prospect Point, and the totem poles at Brockton Point. Pack a gourmet picnic from a local deli or have your hotel prepare a luxury picnic basket to enjoy at one of the park's scenic ocean-view spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Capilano River Regional Park Forest Bathing Walk: After cycling, transfer by private car (approx. 20 min) to Capilano River Regional Park on the North Shore. Embark on a guided or self-led forest bathing walk through towering Douglas firs and ancient cedars along the river canyon. This mindful nature immersion is deeply restorative and pairs beautifully with the morning's active ride.
day_by_day.evening: North Shore Dining Experience: Stay on the North Shore for dinner at one of its acclaimed restaurants before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Vancouver Harbour Stay – request a premium spread of smoked salmon eggs benedict, fresh BC berries, and locally roasted coffee with harbour views.
meals.lunch: Gourmet hotel-prepared picnic basket or provisions from Thierry Chocolaterie & Patisserie (downtown) enjoyed at Stanley Park's Second Beach or Prospect Point lookout. Include artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: The Lobby Restaurant at Lonsdale Quay (North Vancouver) or Miku North Shore – premium sushi and aburi flame-seared nigiri with mountain views. (~$100–140 pp).

day_by_day.notes: Book the private bike guide or premium rental the evening before through your concierge. The forest bathing walk at Capilano is best done without a strict schedule – allow 1.5–2 hours to fully unwind. Weather in June is generally pleasant but bring a light layer for the forest. A private car or rideshare between Stanley Park and Capilano is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge & Ecology Centre: Drive or arrange a private transfer (approx. 25 min from downtown) to Lynn Canyon Park in North Vancouver. Cross the dramatic free suspension bridge over the rushing canyon below – a less-crowded, equally stunning alternative to Capilano. Explore the Ecology Centre to learn about the old-growth ecosystem, then hike the Twin Falls Trail through moss-draped forest and past cascading waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Richmond Night Market & Authentic Asian Street Food Exploration: Head south to Richmond's Golden Village (approx. 35 min from North Vancouver). Explore the vibrant Asian dining district, visiting acclaimed dim sum restaurants, Taiwanese bubble tea shops, and Hong Kong-style bakeries. If visiting in the evening window, the Richmond Night Market (seasonal May–October) opens at 7 PM – plan your afternoon around this.
day_by_day.evening: Richmond Night Market: Arrive at the Richmond Night Market as it opens. Sample an extraordinary range of authentic Asian street food – Japanese takoyaki, Korean corn dogs, Hong Kong egg waffles, Taiwanese stinky tofu, and fresh mango shaved ice. Soak in the vibrant atmosphere with live entertainment and hundreds of food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Medina Café (Gastown/Downtown) – renowned for their Belgian waffles with house-made coulis, lavender lattes, and shakshuka. Arrive early to beat the queue or book ahead. (~$30–45 pp).
meals.lunch: Pajo's Fish & Chips at Garry Point Park (Richmond) – iconic BC spot serving fresh wild-caught halibut and salmon fish and chips with ocean views. A beloved local institution. (~$25–35 pp).
meals.dinner: Richmond Night Market street food crawl – budget $40–70 pp for a wide variety of premium Asian street food tastings, fresh fruit juices, and desserts across multiple vendors.

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon is free to enter – a wonderful luxury in itself. Wear sturdy walking shoes for the forest trails. The Richmond Night Market runs Thursday–Sunday evenings in summer; confirm the schedule in advance. Uber or a private car is recommended between North Vancouver and Richmond. Consider booking a premium dim sum lunch at HK BBQ Master or Chef Tony Seafood Restaurant in Richmond's Golden Village as an alternative lunch option.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Harbour Morning & Gastown Exploration: Begin your final morning with a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Afterwards, take a short walk to historic Gastown – Vancouver's oldest neighbourhood – and explore its cobblestone streets, boutique shops, and the famous steam clock. Visit local artisan coffee roasters and browse independent galleries showcasing Pacific Northwest Indigenous art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell Culinary Experience & Spa Wind-Down: Treat yourself to a premium farewell lunch at one of Vancouver's most celebrated fine dining establishments. Afterwards, return to the hotel for a relaxing spa treatment or rooftop experience (if available) to close out the trip in true luxury style. Begin packing and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Seawall Walk & Departure Prep: Take one final golden-hour stroll along the Coal Harbour seawall from the hotel, soaking in the mountain and harbour panorama. Enjoy a light farewell dinner before arranging a private car transfer for your onward journey.

meals.breakfast: Extended in-hotel breakfast – indulge in a full luxury spread: eggs prepared to order, smoked BC salmon, fresh fruit, croissants, and premium coffee or tea service with harbour views.
meals.lunch: Hawksworth Restaurant (downtown) – one of Vancouver's most acclaimed fine dining destinations. Seasonal tasting menu highlighting the best of BC's land and sea. Ideal for a celebratory farewell lunch. (~$150–200 pp with wine pairing).
meals.dinner: Light and refined: Botanist Restaurant at Fairmont Pacific Rim – elegant botanical-inspired cocktails and small plates. Perfect for a relaxed, memorable final evening. (~$80–110 pp).

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time should be confirmed with the hotel; many luxury properties offer late check-out upon request – ask your concierge in advance. Store luggage with the hotel if your departure is in the evening. Gastown is walkable from Coal Harbour in under 15 minutes. Consider purchasing local artisan goods or Indigenous art as premium souvenirs from Gastown boutiques. Arrange your departure transfer the night before.
